title: Coarse endpoint concentration at every diverging scale for one-dimensional space-time random walks
support_read_scope: All nine executed finite checker implementations
strongest_verified_claim: For each fixed iid space-time law with 0<p<1 almost surely, every deterministic positive real scale sequence M_N tending to infinity, each fixed epsilon>0 and K>0, the quenched-versus-annealed endpoint full-l1 discrepancy on length-M_N consecutive half-open lattice intervals exceeds epsilon with environmental probability at most C_epsilon,K N^-K eventually, uniformly in each deterministic alignment. N0 may depend on the scale sequence; constants depend on the fixed law.

scope.environment: fixed iid over both space and time; strictly elliptic almost surely; no uniform ellipticity required
scope.walk: one-dimensional discrete-time nearest-neighbor, starts at zero
scope.partitions: deterministic real interval widths M_N tending to infinity, real deterministic alignment, half-open cells
scope.probability: environment probability of a quenched law discrepancy, not sampled walk deviation
scope.quantifiers: fixed epsilon,K; superpolynomial as N tends to infinity; no prescribed divergence rate or monotonicity of M_N
scope.constant_dependence: fixed law allowed; N0 also allowed to depend on M_N sequence

limits: No simultaneous guarantee for environment-selected partitions
No law-uniform estimate near delta=0 arrow environments
No static or correlated environment extension
No uncoarsened pointwise local limit inferred
Novelty, firstness and historical priority unresolved
Not conventional human peer review or a journal acceptance certificate
